scope: Disjoint 30-image holdout for Linux x86_64 + RTX 4060 Laptop native TensorRT mixed FP16/FP32 versus ORT CPU FP32

revision_rationale.v1_status: retained unchanged as a failed over-strict ORT TensorRT EP numerical-equivalence diagnostic
revision_rationale.v2_status: retained unchanged as a failed disjoint ORT TensorRT EP semantic gate and as the regression set used to select the native precision policy
revision_rationale.holdout_rule: v3 uses image indices absent from v1 and v2 and was frozen before any native TensorRT inference on a v3 sample
revision_rationale.tolerance_basis: same immutable semantic gate as v2: one source pixel coordinate bound, IoU 0.90, confidence 0.005, with exact count/class/name
revision_rationale.anti_tuning_rule: v3 samples, limits, provider contract, engine SHA, and precision policy are immutable after the first native v3 run; any first-run failure consumes v3 and requires a newly versioned untouched holdout
revision_rationale.final_engine_freeze: The final class-Sigmoid-only FP16/noTF32 precision policy was selected exclusively against the v2 tuning set. The exact CE2D25F9ABD4370A7E5325777CEB1982E42E82C7A3238C24A48E7FDD264467D2 plan was then built and reloaded with captured evidence before any CPU or native inference on a v3 sample. No v3 sample or result informed either the precision policy or the frozen engine bytes.

publication_limits: Publish native TensorRT performance only if this untouched v3 holdout passes; retain both failed ORT TensorRT EP v1/v2 results beside it.
This proves local WSL2/Linux x86_64 GPU/edge-node execution, not Jetson, native ARM64 GPU, or embedded hardware.
This is implementation correctness on a bounded set, not full-dataset mAP or PyTorch lineage evidence.
